<!-- pr-reviewer: 1fc5104d2af2488bff61fa85c1342be7c63aeb07 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Root cause is right: `theme::apply_to` (theme.rs:382) now writes the token table into both egui theme slots, so the OS appearance can no longer swap in egui's stock visuals. A user who picks a theme via Theme... gets the same behaviour as before; the table just also sits in the inactive slot.
- `painted::row_inks` (painted.rs:191) keeps the ink rule in one place. Tree text, icons and the eye all use it, and the new tests pin 4.5:1 on every row ground in both built-in themes.
- A decision file is included (`docs/decisions/506-tree-contrast.md`), the body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #506`, and `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched.
- No unwrap, expect or panic added. No dependencies, build.rs, scripts or `.github` changes. Layering is respected, since this is UI paint and theme code only.

**Local results (trial-merged with current main, clean merge)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` | 373 passed, 3 failed, 5 ignored. The failures are the known ones on main: `headless_run_succeeds` (no GPU adapter) and `structural::shell_structure_dark/light` ("v0.0.0") |
| `tree_ink`, `colorvision` and theme tests in the lib | 25 passed |
| `--test theme_files` | 14 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The pixel look on a real screen was checked by hand by the contributor (comment above). I did not run the GUI.
- `tree_ink_tests.rs` is registered in `mod.rs` out of alphabetical order next to the other test modules. This is cosmetic only.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 1fc5104d2af2488bff61fa85c1342be7c63aeb07 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Row ink comes from the theme token table (`painted::row_inks`, painted.rs), not a hard-coded grey. Icon and eye are now tinted with the row's own inks instead of a white wash, so they work on any theme.
- `theme::apply_to` writes the table into both egui theme slots, so the OS appearance can no longer swap the theme (root cause of #506).
- The test pins WCAG body contrast (4.5:1, `contrast::BODY`) for every row ink on panel, strip, hover and selection ground in dark and light, and checks both egui slots. No magic RGB.
- Hidden, suffix and selected rows stay distinguishable (dim vs body tier). The dark theme changes only in that hidden rows are brighter (dim instead of faint) and icons take the ink instead of white. Both look intentional and match the contributor's macOS check.
- No snapshot PNG or golden changes; no unwrap/expect/panic; provenance line on the new test module; decision file present; body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #506`; no CHANGELOG edit.

**Local results (merged with main, clean trial merge)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-ui --lib` filter `tree_ink` | 2 passed |
| filter `theme` | 16 passed |
| filter `browser` | 5 passed |
| filter `painted` | 0 matched |
| filter `structural` | 1 passed, 2 failed (below) |
| `clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

The two failures are `shell_structure_dark/light`, which expect the label `v0.15.0 · test` but the shell paints `v0.0.0`. The PR does not touch that code and says the same two tests fail on main. Not caused by this PR.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The tests only cover the two built-in themes. Named, file and colour-vision themes are not measured, but they go through the same `row_inks` and `apply_to` path.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
